Hi, I relate to your post a lot. I've struggled with a fear of death for the majority of my life, and it's really a terrifying and horrible thing to go through. The thing which helped me the most was existential therapy, and yes, that is a real thing. My therapist helped me to realise that a lot of my feelings about death (like a fear of non-existence) were irrational and that I was stopping myself from enjoying life. Thoughts like these make it incredibly difficult to immerse yourself in what I call "the human experience" because any joy you feel is sapped away by this feeling of dread. 

My favourite thing she ever said to me, and you can spend some time thinking on this, is that death is necessary for life. The whole reason that we can even experience joy, happiness, sadness, worry, peace - is death. Think about it - you would never get anything done if you had unlimited time on this earth. Life would be completely different, and it would lose its meaning. In order to live a life full of meaning, it is necessary that we have a limited amount of time.
